messages:
Samir Patel: Quick follow-up from the SLO/capacity shapes RFC — we prototyped moving most RBAC checks out of the query runtime into the access-router. Thoughts?
Maya Chen: curious on perf gains. numbers?
Samir Patel: ran a microbench: removing per-request principal checks in query path shaved ~4-6ms p95 on short dashboard queries (250-500 tokens), and reduced CPU jitter under burst.
Jordan (ENG): that's promising. Where do we put caching then? access-router should return effective-principal + allowed-filters header so query layer can cache by auth key.
Lee: worry: that leaks auth logic into router, becoming a hot-path. router is already memory-heavy for tenant mapping.
Aditya: agreed. we can push policy evaluation to a separate auth-service with async cache and short TTLs. router calls it but also has local LRU for top-k tenants.
Tess: operationally, this changes rollout. need canary by tenant + opt-in. we can't break delegated-access customers.
Samir Patel: proposal: 1) Access-router does coarse checks + returns auth-hash header. 2) Query runtime does a single lookup against auth-cache using auth-hash. 3) Auth-service handles policy eval + invalidation hooks. 4) Canary start with 1% tenants, 2-stage flag.
Maya Chen: config sketch:
```json
{"access_router": {"auth_ttl_ms": 5000, "auth_cache_size": 50000}, "query_runtime": {"lookup_mode": "fast_key"}}
```
Jordan (ENG): how do we handle re-evaluation on permission change? Admin changes should invalidate quickly.
Aditya: auth-service will publish invalidation events to ringpop topic; router and query nodes subscribe and evict.
Samir Patel: rollout plan: feature-flag + per-tenant whitelists, probe dashboards, check SLO regressions, revert if p95 increases > 3ms for any tenant.
ops-bot: deploy canary triggered for tenant list: [team-alpha].
deploy-bot: canary started on 2025-10-03T14:12Z — watch logs: /ops/canary.
Tess: add alert: auth-cache-hit-rate < 95% => pause rollout.
Lee: one more: RBAC policy complexity — for complex attribute-based rules we should fallback to runtime check to avoid false negatives.
Samir Patel: yes fallback allowed, but it's rare. we'll track fallback-rate metric. If > 0.5% on prod, pause.
Maya Chen: ok let's sync tomorrow for data we'll collect during canary. short agenda: histograms, fallback rate, p95 delta.
Samir Patel: SGTM. Thanks.
